records.name: País Vasco/Euskadi
records.summary: No region-specific law or incident series diverges from the national framework, but the country dossier records a mixed finding for this community: with Navarra it tops the state hate-crime statistics (highest per-capita LGTBI-motivated offence rates in the 2024 Interior report) — a result the dossier attributes to intensive reporting and counting, not to danger: the regional government runs its own LGTBI public-order police and an equality observatory maintaining a comparative legislation database, and no Basque statute rollback exists. Net visitor risk is assessed at approximately the national score, with the high recorded counts read as neutral-to-positive.

records.name: Comunidad Foral de Navarra
records.summary: No region-specific law or incident series diverges from the national framework, but the country dossier records a mixed finding for this community: it is the single highest per-capita LGTBI hate-offence region in the 2024 Interior report — a result the dossier reads as a reporting-institution effect, since Pamplona runs an annual anti-LGTBIphobia observatory whose 2025 report documents rising discourse, and the region polices public order with its own force. Net visitor risk is assessed at approximately the national score, with the high recorded counts read as reporting quality rather than a safety deficit.

records.name: Región de Murcia
records.summary: Assessed materially in line with the national position. Regional LGTBI or equality legislation is recorded for this region in the national policy inventories, but no region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the dedicated country dossier for this region; no sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, and the 2023 national trans-equality law's implementation (including its education-facing parts) falls to the regional government. The national victimisation baseline applies here: a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident.

records.name: Galicia
records.summary:
Spain's Law 4/2023 for the real and effective equality of trans people (official gazette text) vests implementation of its administrative and education-facing provisions in the autonomous communities — this region's government among them. The parallel 2023 gender-recognition reform, letting registry entries change by self-declaration from age 12 without medical diagnosis, drew an international rights organisation to rank the country among autonomy-first jurisdictions.

The surviving record adds no Galician statute, ordinance, enforcement series or incident finding; regional value here is implementation posture under the 2023 framework, not separate restriction or separate protection.

records.name: Extremadura
records.summary:
Spain's Law 4/2023 (gazette text) leaves implementation of the national trans-equality and self-declaration provisions to the autonomous communities, including this region's government; the 2023 registry reform won the country placement in an international organisation's autonomy-first grouping. The record adds no Extremadura statute, ordinance, enforcement series or incident finding.

This region stands out in national statistics for the LOWEST per-capita recorded rate of hate offences — and the record's own caveat is that the figure reflects how little is counted rather than demonstrated protection. The low number should not be read as reassurance; exposure otherwise tracks the national framework.

records.name: Cataluña/Catalunya
records.summary: Assessed materially in line with the national position. No region-specific adverse incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the country dossier for this region (it sits outside the general inventory's flagged set). no region-specific incident, ordinance or enforcement finding was identified in the dedicated country dossier for this region; no sub-national facility, expression or assembly restriction exists anywhere in the country, and the 2023 national trans-equality law's implementation (including its education-facing parts) falls to the regional government. The national victimisation baseline applies here: a 2026 federation report found 44% of LGTBI respondents had experienced a hate-motivated incident. The region does contain one of the country's densest, most visible LGTBI urban centres with dedicated hate-crime structures within its own regional police force - the dossier's overall point being that in this country the fault line is city-versus-rural, not region-versus-region.
